value.answer: Short term, at low doses (5 mg or less a night) for short periods, it looks fine for most adults. The common side effects are headache and feeling drowsy, and they go away when you stop. Long term is the unclear part. A preliminary heart study from the AHA last November linked a year or more of use in people with insomnia to more heart failure, but it can't prove melatonin caused it, and a later 2026 analysis found no significant link, so the long-term picture still isn't settled. Some sources also flag interactions with blood thinners and antidepressants, so if you take either, check with a doctor or pharmacist first.
